newsitem.title: USA: Fluor abandons 20 pct earnings growth goal.
newsitem.headline: Fluor abandons 20 pct earnings growth goal.

text.p: Flour Corp said Wednesday it is no longer "prudent to pursue" its goal of achieving 20 percent earnings growth this year.
Chief executive officer Les McGraw said the company instead will focus on maintaining its position in the top quartile of S&P 500 companies by improving its profit margin.

McGraw's statements followed the release of disappointing second quarter results for Fluor and its principal subsidiary, the construction and engineering company Fluor Daniel. Fluor posted a net loss of $70.1 million in the second quarter and has lost $8.1 million for the year to date.
The company said it expects Fluor Daniel to turn an operating profit of $140 million in the second half of fiscal 1997. Fluor Daniel reported an operating loss of $36 million in the first half.
"Our entire team is focused on taking immediate and comprehensive corrective actions to improve performance by increasing selectivity, reducing costs and strengthening margins," McGraw said.
Fluor Daniel said the company's $100 million cost reduction program should be completed by year end.
McGraw said Fluor's A.T. Massey Coal unit is poised to benefit from greater deregulation of the electric utility industry and from more stringent environmental standards.
